stimulus_db:
Figorian Wildlife Commission: The development of wetlands in industrialized nations for residential and commercial uses has endangered many species. To protect wildlife we must regulate such development in Figoria: future wetland development must be offset by the construction of replacement wetland habitats. Thus, development would cause no net reduction of wetlands and pose no threat to the species that inhabit them.

Figorian Development Commission: Other nations have flagrantly developed wetlands at the expense of wildlife. We have conserved. Since Figorian wetland development might not affect wildlife and is necessary for growth, we should allow development. We have as much right to govern our own resources as countries that have already put their natural resources to commercial use.
stem_db: Which one of the following principles, if accepted, would most strongly support the Figorian Development Commission's position against the Figorian Wildlife Commission's position?

choices_db.A: National resources should be regulated by international agreement when wildlife is endangered.
choices_db.B: The right of future generations to have wildlife preserved supersedes the economic needs of individual nations.
choices_db.C: Only when a reduction of populations of endangered species by commercial development has been found should regulation be implemented to prevent further damage.
choices_db.D: Environment regulation must aim at preventing any further environmental damage and cannot allow for the different degrees to which different nations have already harmed the environment.
choices_db.E: It is imprudent to allow further depletion of natural resources.

bank.stem: Which one of the following principles, if accepted, would most strongly support the Figorian Development Commission’s position against the Figorian Wildlife Commission’s position?

choices.A: National resources should be regulated by international agreement when wildlife is endangered.
choices.B: The right of future generations to have wildlife preserved supersedes the economic needs of individual nations.
choices.C: Only when a reduction of populations of endangered species by commercial development has been found should regulation be implemented to prevent further damage.
choices.D: Environmental regulation must aim at preventing any further environmental damage and cannot allow for the different degrees to which different nations have already harmed the environment.
choices.E: It is imprudent to allow further depletion of natural resources.

steps.label: Wildlife Commission Conclusion
steps.body: Future wetland development in Figoria must be regulated and offset by replacement habitats so that there is no net reduction of wetlands and no threat to species.

steps.label: Wildlife Commission Evidence
steps.body: Wetland development in industrialized nations has endangered many species.

steps.label: Development Commission Conclusion
steps.body: Figoria should be allowed to develop its wetlands.

steps.label: Development Commission Evidence
steps.body: Figoria has already conserved (unlike other nations that flagrantly developed wetlands), the development might not affect wildlife, and it is necessary for growth. Figoria has the same right to govern its own resources as nations that already used theirs commercially.

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.body:
We're trying to support the second speaker, whose agenda is "let us develop wetlands at the expense of wildlife".
They're kind of saying, "Why do WE have to be the responsible nation that protects these wetland species. It's costing us economically. Other nations have derived commercial benefit from their natural resources. We should be allowed to do the same. We need this for growth and it might not even affect wildlife."

steps.label: Goal
steps.body: We have a lot of premises to work with, and the correct answer doesn't have to use all of them. We just want an answer that takes us FROM something we know is applicable to the FDC's argument helps us take us TO the idea that it's okay to develop wetlands at the expense of wildlife.

notes.body: The Development Commission insists Figoria has the right to govern its own resources. Handing regulation to an international agreement takes that right away. A works against the commission it is supposed to help.
If future generations' right to wildlife outranks a nation's economic needs, the Development Commission's appeal to growth loses. That's the Wildlife Commission's side.

Regulate only after commercial development has actually been found to reduce endangered species. The Development Commission says Figoria has conserved, and its development "might not affect wildlife." So no such harm has been found, and regulation isn't justified yet. The Wildlife Commission wants regulation before any harm, which this principle rules out.

This is the trap, picked by 12%. It talks about how different nations have harmed the environment to different degrees. That's the Development Commission's theme, so it feels like their answer. But read what it concludes: regulation cannot allow for those differences. The commission's whole complaint is that Figoria's record of conserving should count. D says it doesn't.
If further depletion is imprudent, developing the wetlands is imprudent. That supports the Wildlife Commission.
